title: BC stream crossings under the Water Sustainability Act
description: One stream crossing at a time: which authority the change in and about a stream it makes rests on (a culvert, bridge, ford, ice bridge or snowfill), and the conditions the Water Sustainability Regulation sets for it: the forest route of WSR §39(2), a change §39(1) lists with its notice to a habitat officer, or a change approval. A crossing release: the block planner keeps one answer set per crossing it lists, and every answer is the reviewer’s. Release 1.0.0 answered once for the whole block, for its worst crossing.

relatedPacks.relationship: WSR §39(2) authorizes a forest crossing only while it complies with FRPA and its regulations; FPPR §§55–57, 72 and 73 for the same crossing are reviewed in that pack, beside this one.
The block review asks whether the block’s roads or harvesting change a stream at all, and to list each crossing; each listed crossing is answered here.

facts.label: Will this crossing make a change in and about a stream: a culvert, bridge, ford, ice bridge, snowfill or other work in a stream channel or modifying a stream, a wetland, spring or dry channel included (Water Sustainability Act §1)?
Is the change made under WSR §39(2): a change to which a FRPA standard applies, made by a Forest Act agreement or road use permit holder, a Range Act agreement holder or the Crown?
Is the change made instead as a change WSR §39(1) lists (a culvert, clear span bridge, temporary ford, ice bridge, winter ford, snowfill or drainage outlet), by someone §39(2) does not cover?
Is the change made under a change approval, another authorization or an order (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)(a), (c), (d))?

Is the change relied on under §39(2) made by a person it names: a holder of a Forest Act agreement or road use permit, a Range Act agreement or a special use permit, a person authorized to build the road under the Coal, Geothermal Resources, Mining Right of Way or Petroleum and Natural Gas Act, or the Crown?
Will the change comply with FRPA and its regulations and standards (FPPR §§55–57 on stream crossings, fish passage and fish habitat among them)?
Has an engineer required an application for a change approval or authorization for this change, because it may have a significant adverse impact on the stream, its flow or its channel (WSR §37(2))?

Has a habitat officer given written terms for this change (a timing window, minimum flow, removal or addition of material, fish and wildlife salvage, protection of vegetation, worksite restoration; WSR §44(2))?
Is the work planned and scheduled within those terms?
Is the change approval, authorization or order relied on issued, and is the work planned within its terms and conditions?
Was a signed notice of the change’s particulars given to a habitat officer at least 45 days before the work begins (WSR §38(1)(a))?
Has a habitat officer’s statement of the terms on which the change can proceed been obtained (WSR §38(1)(b))?
Have 45 days passed since a habitat officer received the notice without the officer making contact (WSR §38(4))?
Is the change under §39(1) a culvert for a road, trail or footpath (§39(1)(a))?
Equivalent diameter of the culvert
Depth of fill cover over the culvert
Fill height above the top of the culvert
Does the culvert have the stream channel’s hydraulic capacity, or pass the 1 in 200 year maximum daily flow without the water at its inlet rising above its top (§39(1)(a)(vii))?
Is the stream the culvert crosses fish-bearing, with a fish population present at some time in the year (WSR §36)?
Does the culvert let fish pass up and down stream under all flow conditions?
Is the culvert of 2 m or greater equivalent diameter, or designed to pass a flow of more than 6 m³ a second?
Is the culvert designed by an engineering professional and built to that design?

Will the culvert meet the rest of §39(1)(a): equipment in a dry channel or operated from the top of the bank, erosion protection at the inlet and outlet, debris passing through, a stable channel, no backwater or raised head, obstacles and debris removable, the channel outside the right of way unaltered, fill kept off the inlet and outlet, and CSA materials?
Is the change under §39(1) a clear span bridge (§39(1)(b))?

Will the clear span bridge meet §39(1)(b): equipment in a dry channel or operated from the top of the bank, no backwater or raised head, the channel’s hydraulic capacity or the 1 in 200 year maximum daily flow, room under it for flood debris and ice, and CSA materials?
Is the change under §39(1) a temporary ford for vehicles (§39(1)(v))?

Will the temporary ford meet §39(1)(v): built and removed when that risks no significant harm to fish, wildlife or the aquatic ecosystem, holding the 1 in 10 year maximum daily flow without loss or channel erosion, any culvert passing the average low flow, the channel protected from erosion during use and after removal, no sediment from approach ditches, an erosion-free running surface, the stream in its channel and debris passing over it?
Is the change under §39(1) an ice bridge, winter ford or snowfill (§39(1)(n))?

Will it be built only of clean ice and snow removed from the channel before ice breakup, with an ice bridge’s logs, timber and other materials removed before breakup without a significant risk of harm?
